warnings.value: Ritonavir is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor — its main modern clinical role is as a pharmacokinetic 'booster' for other antiretrovirals, but this means it carries an unusually large drug-interaction list that must always be checked before adding any new medicine. GI upset and lipid abnormalities with long-term use are also recognised.

counsellingPoints.value: Tell every prescriber and pharmacist that you're on ritonavir before starting any new medicine — the interaction risk is genuinely high.

warnings.value: Hepatotoxicity risk rises with age and alcohol use. Peripheral neuropathy risk relates to pyridoxine (vitamin B6) depletion, which is why pyridoxine is commonly co-prescribed during treatment. Some MAO-inhibiting activity means a tyramine reaction is possible with tyramine-rich foods/alcohol.

foodLifestyle.value: Take on an empty stomach for best absorption; avoid alcohol and tyramine-rich foods.

clinicalPearls.value: Co-prescribing pyridoxine specifically to prevent isoniazid-induced peripheral neuropathy is a classic TB-treatment teaching point.

counsellingPoints.value: Avoid alcohol. Take on an empty stomach. Report any tingling or numbness in the hands or feet.

overdoseEarlySigns.value: Blurred vision or colour-vision changes are the key early warning sign, not a general GI symptom.

overdoseSevereSigns.value: Any visual change needs the drug stopped promptly and urgent medical assessment — this is not a 'wait and see' symptom.

antidoteOrSupportive.value: No specific antidote — stopping the drug promptly on visual symptoms is the primary management, under medical direction.

clinicalPearls.value: Ethambutol's optic neuritis risk is the textbook reason visual monitoring is built into standard TB treatment follow-up.

counsellingPoints.value: Report any change in vision — blurring or altered colour vision — immediately, rather than waiting for the next appointment.

warnings.value: Hyperkalaemia risk, especially with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or potassium-sparing diuretics. Rare but serious skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome/TEN) can occur. In HIV care this drug is often used as long-term prophylaxis rather than a short course, so these risks apply over a longer exposure window.

lessons.title: Expected colour change
lessons.body: Orange-red urine, tears, and sweat can alarm patients. Teaching that this is expected improves adherence — educational framing only.

lessons.title: Why ART + TB is high stakes
lessons.body: Rifampicin induces drug-metabolising enzymes. Some ART exposures fall — Materia flags the interaction educationally and refuses to invent dose changes.

quiz.prompt: A patient on rifampicin and dolutegravir asks if orange urine means kidney damage. Best educational frame?
choices: Orange-red fluids are an expected rifampicin effect — still escalate new pain/oliguria clinically; do not invent a dose change
It means the TB is cured
